title: pqch.attestation/1 — a supplier's statement about its products' cryptography, brought in as reported evidence
description: What a hardware or software supplier attests about a product at a version: the algorithms its firmware is signed with, its secure-boot chain, its TPM, the validated modules it carries, its post-quantum roadmap and whether the installed version can be updated, must be replaced or has no statement. Imported by `pqch attest` as `attestation.recorded` events, graded `reported`: a document the workbench did not watch being made. It never outranks what the server itself showed; where the two differ, the difference is recorded.

supplier.description: Who attests: the supplier's name as it signs the statement.

reference.description: Where the statement is published or who issued it (a URL, a document number, a contact).

illustrative.description: True when the document is a worked example and not the supplier's own statement; every page that shows it says so.

vendor.description: The device's manufacturer as its firmware reports it (DMI sys_vendor, Redfish Manufacturer).

model.description: The model as the firmware reports it (DMI product_name, Redfish Model). Matched case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed.

where.description: Which part of the product uses it: the controller's firmware, the BIOS, the operating system image.

cmvp_certificate.description: The CMVP certificate number, or null when the module is not validated.

name.description: The firmware's name as the server reports it (`BIOS`, the controller's inventory name). Matched case-insensitively.

version.description: The version the statement is about, or `any` for every version of this firmware on this model.

signing.description: How the firmware image itself is signed: what the platform verifies before it runs.

secure_boot_chain.description: The certificate authorities the shipped databases trust, by subject.

tls.description: For a firmware with its own listeners (a management controller): what its TLS and SSH offer.

post_quantum.description: The supplier's roadmap for this firmware: which algorithms, in which version, by when; `available: null` means no date is given.

supportability.description: What the supplier says of the installed firmware's route to post-quantum algorithms: an update exists or is planned; the hardware must be replaced; the product is past support; or the supplier makes no statement.
